atoms.b:
The four waves of industrialisation

The First Industrial Revolution (1760–1900) began with the ((invention --digitalisation)) of the steam engine, which enabled companies to produce goods in large ((factories --fields)). Societies that had previously relied mainly on agriculture therefore became increasingly ((industrial --manufactured)).
The second wave of industrialisation (1900–1970) was marked by the invention of the assembly line, which made ((mass --digital)) production faster and more efficient.

During the third wave of industrialisation (1970–2000), ((automation --communication)) through computers and robots increased. This enabled traditional industrial societies with a high number of ((working --upper))-class people to become ((service --agricultural)) economies.
The fourth wave (since 2000) is also known as the digital revolution. It replaced many analogue technologies with ((digital --electronic)) ones.
